title: UPI Gets a Price: What 0.4% MDR Means for Banks and Fintechs

shorts.title: The margin is not the moat

beats.say: From the fifteenth of October, UPI gets a price. Merchants will pay a merchant discount rate of zero point four percent on UPI payments above two thousand rupees, capped at three hundred rupees a payment.
beats.cap: From 15 October, UPI gets a price. Merchants will pay a Merchant Discount Rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 a payment.
cues: From 15 October, UPI gets a price.
Merchants will pay a Merchant Discount Rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above
₹2,000, capped at ₹300 a payment.

beats.say: Banks and payment companies will earn a margin on part of the largest flow of payments in the country. But a margin set by a committee is not a moat. The moat is whoever owns the merchant.
beats.cap: Banks and payment companies will earn a margin on part of the largest flow of payments in the country. But a margin set by a committee is not a moat. The moat is whoever owns the merchant.

items.text: A MARGIN SET BY A COMMITTEE

cues: Banks and payment companies will earn a margin on part of the largest flow of
payments in the country.

beats.say: Chapter one. What NPCI announced.
beats.cap: Chapter one. What NPCI announced.
cues: Chapter one.
What NPCI announced.

beats.say: NPCI's F A Q of the fifteenth of September sets it out. Payments up to two thousand rupees stay free. Above that, the merchant pays zero point four percent. From seventy five thousand rupees, the fee is capped at three hundred rupees.
beats.cap: NPCI's FAQ of 15 September sets it out. Payments up to ₹2,000 stay free. Above that, the merchant pays 0.4%. From ₹75,000, the fee is capped at ₹300.
cues: NPCI's FAQ of 15 September sets it out.
Payments up to ₹2,000 stay free.
Above that, the merchant pays 0.4%.
From ₹75,000, the fee is capped at ₹300.

beats.say: Insurance premiums, fuel, utilities, railways and telecom pay a flat five rupees. Capital market payments pay zero point zero two percent. Person to person payments, AutoPay mandates and small merchants stay free.
beats.cap: Insurance premiums, fuel, utilities, railways and telecom pay a flat ₹5. Capital market payments pay 0.02%, capped at ₹300. Person-to-person payments, AutoPay mandates and small merchants stay free.
cues: Insurance premiums, fuel, utilities, railways and telecom pay a flat ₹5.
Capital market payments pay 0.02%, capped at ₹300.
Person-to-person payments, AutoPay mandates and small merchants stay free.

beats.say: In NPCI's own example, a three thousand rupee purchase costs the merchant twelve rupees. Consumers pay nothing, merchants may not pass the charge on, and payment apps may not add a platform fee.
beats.cap: In NPCI's own example, a ₹3,000 purchase costs the merchant ₹12. Consumers pay nothing, merchants may not pass the charge on, and payment apps may not add a platform fee.
cues: In NPCI's own example, a ₹3,000 purchase costs the merchant ₹12.
Consumers pay nothing, merchants may not pass the charge on,
and payment apps may not add a platform fee.

beats.say: The scale is huge. In August alone, UPI processed two thousand four hundred and fifty one crore transactions, worth twenty nine point nine lakh crore rupees. Payments up to two thousand rupees are more than ninety five percent of merchant transactions by volume. NPCI does not publish their share by value.
beats.cap: The scale is huge. In August 2026 alone, UPI processed 2,451 crore transactions, worth ₹29.9 lakh crore. Payments up to ₹2,000 are more than 95% of merchant (P2M) transactions by volume. NPCI does not publish their share by value.
cues: The scale is huge.
In August 2026 alone, UPI processed 2,451 crore transactions,
worth ₹29.9 lakh crore.
Payments up to ₹2,000 are more than 95% of merchant (P2M) transactions by
volume.
NPCI does not publish their share by value.

beats.cap: Chapter two. The margin.

beats.say: NPCI says the fee is distributed only amongst the UPI ecosystem, and cites an industry estimate that running UPI costs about twenty thousand crore rupees a year. But it does not say who gets what. A steering committee headed by NPCI decides the split.
beats.cap: NPCI says the MDR "is distributed only amongst the UPI ecosystem", and cites an industry estimate that running UPI costs "around ~₹20,000 crore annually". But it does not say who gets what. A steering committee headed by NPCI decides the split.
cues: NPCI says the MDR "is distributed only amongst the UPI ecosystem",
and cites an industry estimate that running UPI costs "around ~₹20,000 crore
annually".
But it does not say who gets what.
A steering committee headed by NPCI decides the split.

beats.say: Paytm told the exchanges the change will generate additional revenue from payments that were free earlier.
beats.cap: Paytm told the exchanges the change "will generate additional revenue from the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free earlier".
cues: Paytm told the exchanges the change "will generate additional revenue from
the merchant business for many of the payment transactions that were free
earlier".

beats.say: Compare that with Paytm's economics. In the June quarter, its merchant payment value was seven point one lakh crore rupees, and its payment processing margin was just above four basis points. The new fee is forty basis points gross. Even a small share of it matters.
beats.cap: Compare that with Paytm's economics. In Q1 FY27, its merchant GMV was ₹7.1 lakh crore, and its payment processing margin was "comfortably above 4bps". The new MDR is 40 basis points gross. Even a small share of it matters.
cues: Compare that with Paytm's economics.
In Q1 FY27, its merchant GMV was ₹7.1 lakh crore,
and its payment processing margin was "comfortably above 4bps".
The new MDR is 40 basis points gross.
Even a small share of it matters.

beats.say: Chapter three. Why the margin is not the moat.
beats.cap: Chapter three. Why the margin is not the moat.
cues: Chapter three.
Why the margin is not the moat.

beats.say: MoatSCORE asks whether a company controls its own price. Here, nobody does. The rate is set centrally, the split by a committee, merchants cannot pass it on, and apps cannot add fees. What a committee grants, a committee can change. MoatSCORE tracks that as ungoverned risk, and never scores it.
beats.cap: MoatSCORE asks whether a company controls its own price. Here, nobody does. The rate is set centrally, the split by a committee, merchants cannot pass it on, and apps cannot add fees. What a committee grants, a committee can change. MoatSCORE tracks that as Ungoverned Risk (D8), and never scores it.
cues: MoatSCORE asks whether a company controls its own price.
Here, nobody does.
The rate is set centrally, the split by a committee,
merchants cannot pass it on, and apps cannot add fees.
What a committee grants, a committee can change.
MoatSCORE tracks that as Ungoverned Risk (D8), and never scores it.

beats.say: The focus moat is switching costs: the merchant relationship. Every provider earns the same regulated rate. What differs is how many merchants each has signed up, and how hard it is for them to leave. Paytm has one point five seven crore merchants on subscription plans, including devices.
beats.cap: The focus moat is switching costs: the merchant relationship. Every provider earns the same regulated rate. What differs is how many merchants each has signed up, and how hard it is for them to leave. Paytm has 1.57 crore merchants on subscription plans, including devices.

the merchant relationship.
Every provider earns the same regulated rate.
What differs is how many merchants each has signed up,
and how hard it is for them to leave.
Paytm has 1.57 crore merchants on subscription plans, including devices.

beats.say: The fee does not create a moat. It raises the value of one that already exists, the installed merchant base, and funds the race to build it.
beats.cap: The MDR does not create a moat. It raises the value of one that already exists, the installed merchant base, and funds the race to build it.

beats.say: Chapter four. What it means for banks.
beats.cap: Chapter four. What it means for banks.
cues: Chapter four.
What it means for banks.

beats.say: Banks sit on both sides of every UPI payment. For them, the fee is mainly cost recovery, replacing government subsidy that NPCI calls short term bridge funding.
beats.cap: Banks sit on both sides of every UPI payment. For them, the MDR is mainly cost recovery, replacing government subsidy that NPCI calls "short-term bridge funding".
cues: Banks sit on both sides of every UPI payment.
For them, the MDR is mainly cost recovery,
replacing government subsidy that NPCI calls "short-term bridge funding".

beats.say: Credit on UPI is separate. RuPay credit cards on UPI stay under card rules, where fees are one and a half to two and a half percent. Even at zero point four percent, UPI stays cheaper than a debit card, at up to zero point nine percent.
beats.cap: Credit on UPI is separate. RuPay credit cards on UPI stay under card rules, where MDRs are 1.5% to 2.5%. Even at 0.4%, UPI stays cheaper than a debit card, at up to 0.90%.
cues: Credit on UPI is separate.
RuPay credit cards on UPI stay under card rules, where MDRs are 1.5% to 2.5%.
Even at 0.4%, UPI stays cheaper than a debit card, at up to 0.90%.

beats.say: The bear case. The rate can move. Merchants may route around it by staying below two thousand rupees. The money may be competed away on devices. And if banks take most of the split, apps may see little of it.
beats.cap: The bear case. The rate can move. Merchants may route around it by staying below ₹2,000. The money may be competed away on devices. And if banks take most of the split, apps may see little of it.

The rate can move.

The money may be competed away on devices.
And if banks take most of the split, apps may see little of it.
